blocks.text: State can choose between two simple views while learning. A real navigation library adds history and platform navigation behaviour for larger apps.
Use a current Expo project with React Native. Put examples in App.jsx. Run the project with Expo on a supported device or emulator. Native components do not run in this website's HTML playground.

blocks.code:
import {useState} from "react";import {View,Text,Button} from "react-native";
export default function App(){const [detail,setDetail]=useState(false);return <View style={{padding:24}}>{detail?<><Text>Moon Trip is a space story.</Text><Button title="Back" onPress={()=>setDetail(false)}/></>:<><Text>Books</Text><Button title="Open Moon Trip" onPress={()=>setDetail(true)}/></>}</View>;}
blocks.title: Make a local two-view demo

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `onPress` is the native action callback. It is different from a web button's `onClick` prop.
`useState` gives React a remembered value and a setter. Call the setter to ask React to show the next value.

blocks.text: The buttons switch between a list label and a book detail view within local state.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: This small switch is not a full navigation system. It does not implement deep links or platform back history.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Add a second sentence to the detail view.
